scenario.title: Carrier rejects shipment notices
scenario.initial_request: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them

M-REJECT-COUNT-STRUCTURAL.name: Count of rejected shipment notices by structural reason (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER)
M-REJECT-COUNT-STRUCTURAL.population: rejected shipment notices recorded in reject-log

M-RESUBMIT-RECURRENCE-RATE.name: Rate of resubmitted notices rejected again for the same reason
M-RESUBMIT-RECURRENCE-RATE.numerator: resubmitted notices rejected again with the same reject reason
M-RESUBMIT-RECURRENCE-RATE.denominator: total notices resubmitted following a prior reject

F-01.statement: reject-log rejects_by_reason returned 3 rejected notices: N-1 and N-2 reason LOC_UNKNOWN, N-3 reason EVENT_ORDER.

CL-01.statement: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them

CL-02.statement: The carrier system is flaky; just resubmit everything.

H-NOTICE-CONTENT-ERRORS.statement: Shipment notices from Shipper (ORG-A) contain data errors that cause Carrier (ORG-B) to reject them, and these errors are mechanically correctable, so an auto-fix-and-resubmit agent would resolve the root cause.

H-CARRIER-RULE-MISMATCH.statement: Rejects are driven by Carrier-side business rules or reference data (e.g. stale master data, overly strict validation) that flag otherwise-valid notices, meaning the fix belongs on ORG-B's side, not in a shipper-side auto-fix bot.

H-REJECT-LOG-MEASUREMENT-GAP.statement: The scale or nature of the reject problem is mis-scoped because DA-REJ's completeness is UNKNOWN, so the true root cause and magnitude cannot yet be established from this data asset alone.

H-UPSTREAM-PROCESS-RECURRENCE.statement: Rejects stem from a recurring upstream data-entry or process issue in P-1 (shipment notice process) at the Shipper, which needs a process/training fix rather than a per-instance AI auto-fix.

H-BLIND-RESUBMIT-INEFFECTIVE.statement: Blanket resubmission of rejected notices without correcting the underlying LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER causes seen in E-01 would likely just reproduce the same rejects, since those causes are structural, not transient carrier-system flakiness.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The reject-log breakdown shows only 3 rejected notices, with reasons LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (N-3) — not generic content typos. This is the first authoritative, complete look at actual reject reasons, and it does not obviously match the stakeholder's framing of "correctable content errors."

E-02.content: The carrier system is flaky; just resubmit everything.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-REQ (non-authoritative, interview) now attributes rejects to a 'flaky' carrier system and proposes blanket resubmission, a different framing than their own earlier claim of correctable content errors (CL-01). This framing also does not match the authoritative reject-log reasons (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER in E-01), which point to specific data/sequencing issues rather than carrier system instability.

U-FIX-OWNERSHIP-SIDE.question: Do LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER rejects originate from Shipper-side process/data entry (P-1) or Carrier-side validation rules/reference data (ORG-B)?
U-FIX-OWNERSHIP-SIDE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation targets ORG-A's notice-generation process or ORG-B's validation rules, which are different fixes with different owners.
U-FIX-OWNERSHIP-SIDE.resolution_path: Compare N-1/N-2/N-3 notice contents against P-1 process steps and against ORG-B's current validation rules/reference data.
U-FIX-OWNERSHIP-SIDE.safe_placeholder: Route rejected notices to manual review by both ORG-A and ORG-B contacts rather than auto-fixing on one side.

U-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY-AT-SCAL.question: Does the current n=3 reject sample reflect the true volume/trend of rejects, or is it limited by an observation window not yet captured in DA-REJ?
U-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY-AT-SCAL.decision_impact: Affects whether reject-count targets and thresholds are meaningful or need recalibration as more data accumulates.
U-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY-AT-SCAL.resolution_path: Extend reject-log monitoring window and re-run rejects_by_reason over a longer period.
U-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY-AT-SCAL.safe_placeholder: Treat current counts as a preliminary baseline only, not a final target.

A-STRUCTURAL-NOT-FLAKINESS.statement: LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reasons reflect genuine notice data/sequencing issues rather than an undiagnosed Carrier system defect.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE.statement: The 3 logged rejects (N-1, N-2, N-3) are representative of the reject pattern despite DA-REJ's completeness being marked UNKNOWN.

SC-NO-BLIND-RESUBMIT.statement: Any remediation must not blindly auto-correct generic content and resubmit without addressing the actual LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER causes.
SC-NO-BLIND-RESUBMIT.validation_method: Review reject-log rejects_by_reason after remediation to confirm LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER no longer recur for the same input class.

SC-REDUCE-STRUCTURAL-REJECTS.statement: Reduce LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER driven rejects toward zero over time.
SC-REDUCE-STRUCTURAL-REJECTS.validation_method: Track reject-log rejects_by_reason counts over time after remediation.

SC-RESUBMIT-NOT-RECURRING.statement: Resubmitted notices should not recur-reject for the same structural reason.
SC-RESUBMIT-NOT-RECURRING.validation_method: Compare reject reasons before and after resubmission in reject-log.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent that auto-fixes rejected shipment notices and resubmits them to the Carrier automatically (SH-REQ initial request, CL-01).
symptoms: Carrier rejects shipment notices; the only recorded rejects (N-1, N-2, N-3) show reasons LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER, not generic content errors (E-01).

The requester's framing of the reject cause shifted from correctable content errors (CL-01) to carrier-system flakiness (CL-02), and neither matches the authoritative reject-log reasons (C-2, C-4, C-5).
problem_definition.root_problem: Carrier (ORG-B) rejects Shipper (ORG-A) shipment notices specifically because they fail LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER validation checks (N-1, N-2, N-3 per E-01), not because of generic correctable content typos (CL-01, rejected via H-NOTICE-CONTENT-ERRORS) or carrier-system flakiness (CL-02/E-02, non-authoritative, contradicted by E-01). Because these causes are structural rather than transient, blindly auto-correcting and resubmitting notices would likely reproduce the same rejects (H-BLIND-RESUBMIT-INEFFECTIVE).

proposal.summary: The defined problem (PD-1) is that Carrier (ORG-B) rejects Shipper (ORG-A) shipment notices specifically for LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reasons on the only 3 logged rejects (N-1, N-2, N-3 per authoritative evidence E-01) — not the generic 'correctable content errors' the requester originally described (CL-01) nor the 'flaky carrier system' they later claimed (CL-02/E-02), both of which were contradicted by the reject-log data. Because these causes look structural, an auto-fix-and-resubmit bot (the original request) was rejected as a solution (H-NOTICE-CONTENT-ERRORS REJECTED, H-BLIND-RESUBMIT-INEFFECTIVE SUPPORTED); the real open question (U-FIX-OWNERSHIP-SIDE) is whether the fix belongs on the Shipper or Carrier side, and this was deferred as a verification obligation (VOB-U-FIX-OWNERSHIP-SIDE) at a CONDITIONAL_PASS gate. What was released is the completed reject-reason analysis work item (W-WI-ANALYZE-REJECTS), under decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds. The release carries documented limitations because the plan to consult ORG-B's interface owner (SH-INT) to resolve ownership cannot currently execute (no catalog interview tool for SH-INT), the ownership VOB is still open, the sample size (3 notices) is too small to confirm overall scale/trend, and any downstream shipper- or carrier-side fix — plus ORG-B's cooperation if the fault is Carrier-side — remains undesigned and unconfirmed.
